about: The moth's foils, gantry and wand (docs/moth-4). Game frame: x forward from the hull's middle, y to starboard, z up from the design waterline (at rest, sailor aboard), metres. Sizes are the size card's (typical for today's boats: a 'big' main foil of about 1.0 m and 0.12 m^2, an elevator of about 0.7 m); shapes are plain NACA four-digit sections, nothing copied from any builder's foil.

strut.note: the main foil's vertical strut (the daggerboard): through a case in the hull (class rule 6.3.3: it leaves the hull below the waterline), just aft of the mast step; its foot 1.05 m below the hull's lowest point

main_foil.note: a T at the strut's foot, straight quarter-chord line, taper 0.55; the flap (MOTH_Flap) is the aft 30% of the inner 82% of the span, drawn at 0 deg (the game turns it about the FlapHinge socket's axis)

pod.note: the junction's fairing: a slim torpedo that carries the flap's pushrod bellcrank

gantry.note: two carbon tubes from the transom's corners converging to the rudder's stock behind the hull (class rule 6.1.2: removable, and inside the 500 mm allowance of 6.1.5)

rudder.note: a straight vertical blade hung on the gantry; its foot at the same depth as the main foil's

elevator.note: the T at the rudder's foot; the twist grip turns the whole elevator (or the rudder blade's rake) a few degrees, drawn at 0 (the game turns it about ElevatorPivot)

wand.note: hinged on a short bow fitting; drawn in the flying pose, its paddle on the water 0.45 m under the hull's lowest point (the game swings it about WandPivot from the wave height under its tip)
